shamefastness: The quality of being shamefaced; modesty restrained by a sense of propriety.
shamefast: Modest; reserved; restrained by a sense of propriety.
meek: Mild of temper; not easily provoked; given to forbearance under injuries.
bountiful: Free in giving; liberal; generous in bestowing gifts and favors.
conceit: That which is conceived, imagined, or formed in the mind; idea; thought; opinion.
sophist: One of a class of teachers in ancient Greece; hence, a captious or fallacious reasoner.
sophists: Teachers of rhetoric and philosophy in ancient Greece; hence, specious reasoners.
redress: To set right; to remedy; to repair; to relieve from, and to indemnify for, wrong or injury.
auditories: Audiences; assemblies of hearers; also, places where lectures or discourses are delivered.
excessive: Characterized by, or exhibiting, excess; overmuch; beyond the common measure or proportion.
prestidigitator: One skilled in sleight of hand; a juggler.
contemn: To despise; to scorn; to slight; to treat with disdain.
efficacy: Power to produce effects; the power of producing the effect intended; effectiveness.
incidental: Happening as a chance or undesigned feature of something else; casual; not of prime concern.
forbear: To refrain from; to abstain from; to keep away from; to hold oneself back.
diet: Course of living or nourishment; what is eaten and drunk habitually; food regularly taken.
